title: The Price of Good Deeds
text: Just as Father said, there’s no doubt that Éclair died because of our involvement. After all, she was alive in the original world and in the previous timeline.
“So, just to be on the safe side.”
“Yeah. If that’s the case, it’s better to know.”
“What are you talking about?”
“Oh, I hadn’t told the Queen yet. She might already know, but Motoyasu-kun came from the future.”
“That’s right.”

The Queen opened her fan to hide her mouth, as if finding it hard to believe at first, but after a moment, she nodded. Whether she believes it or not is another matter—she’s willing to listen to the story, at least. Compared to Ren and Itsuki, she’s much easier to talk to.
“There’s also testimony from Melty and various other sources. That’s precisely why Mr. Kitamura helped Mr. Iwatani, isn’t it? Considering the situation, that certainly seems to be the case.”
As expected of a Finacée’s parent. Compared to that Crimson Swine’s parent, she has a level of understanding that’s almost hard to believe.

“Anyway, getting back to the topic—it seems that in the future… or should I say, in an ‘alternate’ world? It appears that person, Eclair, isn’t dead. So Motoyasu-kun wants to know how to save her in case the loop happens again.”
“I see… Well then, let me explain the circumstances surrounding how Miss Seaetto died in prison. To be honest, it might be better if you didn’t hear this.”
“Even so, we want to be prepared for the ‘what if.’ Right, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Yes, sir. Since it’s a request from Father, I, Motoyasu, will definitely save her if I get the chance.”
“Understood. Then let me explain what happened. As for how Miss Seaetto died—”
The queen then gave a vivid account of the events leading up to Éclair’s death. Broadly speaking, the cause was that my Father had become far too prominent.

Éclair, so to speak, belonged to a faction of Demi-Humans who worshipped the Shield Hero. With her being held captive in the castle, Father’s exploits were being widely publicized. It was right around the time of the revolution, wasn’t it? I’ve heard that soldiers and knights of the Three Heroes Church, as well as nobles, relentlessly tortured Éclair as a scapegoat.

Moreover, once demands to free Éclair began to surface, they likely felt they could no longer afford to release her. Before eliminating my father—the Shield Hero—the Three Heroes Church killed Éclair, who stood before them as the very embodiment of a traitor to the nation.

Apparently, there had been discussions within the Three Heroes Church about whether to kill her right in front of the Revolutionary Army, but it’s said that Éclair’s own physical strength had already reached its limit before that could happen. Although the “Shadow of the Nation” tried to help her in some way, they couldn’t act recklessly, and Éclair herself—for the sake of those who believed in the Shield Hero, whom she’d only heard about through rumors—chose to die of her own accord… or so the story goes.

The events leading up to that point were so distasteful to hear that my Father was on the verge of covering his ears. However, perhaps because he was resigned to accepting that this was the result of their own actions, he listened until the very end.

“As a result, the Three Heroes Church failed to halt the Revolutionary Army’s advance by taking Seaetto hostage. They were unable to carry out their plan of using her as a spectacle, setting a trap, and slaughtering the entire Revolutionary Army in the meantime.”
“What a cruel way of thinking…”
My father said with a look of regret.
“It’s the rot at the heart of our country… This is all my responsibility.”
My father fell silent. Well, since the Three Heroes Church—the mastermind behind all these events—was ultimately dealt with, I suppose that means Éclair’s grievances have been avenged?
“Please don’t worry too much about it. But if you truly do have the ability to loop, please at least save Seaetto in the next world.”
“Motoyasu-kun, I’m asking you this as well.”
“Understood!”
My Father and the Queen both asked me. That’s right. I’ll do my best to help Éclair as much as I can. It seems she’s surprisingly prone to dying, after all. Of course, that’s assuming I do loop.

I also have my own goal: to find Filo-tan. I haven’t given up on this loop yet, after all. As expected, Filo-tan wasn’t in the egg at the Monster Merchant’s place. Once Ren and Itsuki’s issues are settled, I’ll go look for Filo-tan.
Fortunately, my Father will be starting the reconstruction of the village where Keel is from. In the meantime, I’ll search for Filo-tan.
“So, Mr. Iwatani, how did the leveling go on Cal Mira Island?”
“Ah, about that—we’ve already discussed this, right?”
“Yes. Regarding the movements of Lord Amaki and Lord Kawasumi.”
“Right. Have you found out anything about Ren and Itsuki?”
“The report is that they forced their way onto the last flight the day before, threatened the crew to make the ship set sail, and then vanished without a trace.”
“It’s clear they used a portal or one of the teleportation Skills. What about their whereabouts afterward?”
“Early this morning, there was an eyewitness report of someone matching their description along the eastern border of Melromarc.”

It seems they’ve already begun their journey. However, this is exactly the kind of move I expected. It’s clear beyond a doubt that they’ve begun moving toward the country where the Spirit Tortoise is sealed.
“Based on the testimony, we suspect it’s Lord Kawasumi’s party.”
“Can’t we stop them at the border?”
“It’s not impossible, but there’s a risk they’ll force their way through. Furthermore, there’s a possibility they’ll pretend to be ordinary adventurers.”
“That ‘disguise’ business, huh…”
“It is possible to expose them. There is a precedent from the past where Lord Amaki managed to evade the Three Heroes Church’s vigilance… so it depends on what tactics they use…”
“Come to think of it, how did Ren manage to get out of Melromarc?”
“According to the information we’ve gathered, when Lord Kawasumi set out on an expedition to Zeltoble, Ren subtly tagged along and slipped through.”

Ah, I see. So he crossed the border by tagging along with Itsuki—who was a favorite of the Three Heroes Church—or perhaps he traveled by ship. They probably didn’t want to come on too strong, since treating Ren with discrimination would have made Itsuki suspicious. After that, he stayed in Zeltoble and carried out his activities there, didn’t he?
“For now, I’ll inform the Queen, but Ren and Itsuki are trying to break the Spirit Tortoise’s seal. We must stop them at all costs.”
My father has explained the situation to the Queen. As things stand, Ren and Itsuki have no way of defeating the Spirit Tortoise once its seal is broken. That would result in enormous casualties.
“We’ll have to face Nami, but before that, we need to capture Ren and Itsuki.”
“Understood. It’s a shame—we’d just started building a good relationship, but it seems we’ve meddled where we shouldn’t have. I apologize.”
“No, no… the fault lies with us. It’s nothing the Queen or the people of this world need to worry about.”
After all, he’d stated outright that they would stop it at all costs. I wonder if Ren and Itsuki are just being stubborn now?

“Well, it might be a waste of time, but let’s still issue a warning to his kingdom about obstructing the hero’s visit and advise them to evacuate. In the worst-case scenario, that might help minimize the damage.”
“Please do. And… um, since we might end up facing the Spirit Tortoise, Melty-chan, could you stay behind…”
“Naofumi-sama!”
My finacée spoke up, as if to object.
“I’m one of Naofumi-sama’s companions too! That’s why my mother sent me here!”
“But… this could turn into a very dangerous battle. Since you’re the princess of this kingdom, I thought it would be better for you to stay somewhere safe…”
“Mother! I—I am no longer a princess who just sits quietly and waits! Please! Grant me permission to accompany Lord Naofumi into battle!”
The finacée leaned forward and pleaded with the queen. The queen closed her eyes as if in thought, then opened them and stroked the finacée’s head.

“Melty, you used to be a bit too serious—or perhaps I should say, you tended to hold yourself back—but it seems meeting Lord Iwatani has helped you grow in a positive way. I’m proud of how you’ve grown.”
“Mother… Well then!”
“Yes… It will be a difficult battle, but leading the way for the sake of the world is the duty of royalty. Do your best to be a strength to Lord Iwatani.”
“…Is that all right?”
When Father asks the Queen, she nods.
“Yes. Even if she were to fall before achieving her goal, that would be my fault for sending her off. Lord Iwatani, please take good care of Melty.”
“……I understand. I will do my best to protect your daughter as much as possible.”
Finacée’s expression brightens. Did she look like this in the future?
